key_insight: Machine learning supports wireless power transfer through three connected tasks: structural optimization, state and parameter estimation, and adaptive control.
engineering_relevance: These approaches can help maintain efficient, safe power delivery as geometry, coupling, load, and alignment change.
method: Supervised learning enables fast surrogate models, regression, and classification.
Reinforcement learning addresses sequential control and scheduling.
Hybrid and physics-informed methods combine physical knowledge with data-driven models.
evidence_signal: The abstract provides a qualitative comparison of learning approaches and identifies limited, biased datasets and missing standardized benchmarks, without reporting quantitative performance results.
watch_item: Engineering deployment requires validation of generalization and safety under unseen operating conditions, especially during online adaptation.
paper_title: Machine Learning-Enabled Wireless Power Transfer: A Task-Oriented Review of Structural Optimization, State and Parameter Estimation, and Adaptive Control
